CONVENTION '88
Fostering basic fraternal values proves
to he theme of 145th Convention
(Washington, D.C.) The excitement at the hub of the
nation's government in an election year made Washing
ton D.C. an excellent place for Psi Upsilon to meet for
its convention in August 1988. The Hyatt Arlington Hotel
and its General Manager, Richard Carlson, Epsilon Nu
'69, provided an outstanding "home" for the fraternity
throughout the event.
The excitement began on Thursday, August 25, when
the convention was opened by Stephen T. Selby, Phi
Beta '89, undergraduate president ofthe Phi Beta Chap
ter, host of this year's annual event. A thought-provoking
presentation was given that first evening by Will S. Keim,
who currently is pursuing his Ph.D. at Oregon State
University. "Demythologizing the Animal House," a
moving talk on the role of college fraternities in the
1980's, set the tone for three intense days of work and
play. Representatives from 32 of Psi Upsilon's 33 chap
ters topped off" the evening by attending a festive "Wel
come to Virginia" reception hosted by the members of

the Phi Beta Chapter.
Charting the course for the upcoming year is the
mission that each Psi Upsilon convention sets out to
accomplish. This year the delegates took their respon
sibilities to heart and undertook actions that will not only
affect Psi Upsilon for the coming year but well into the
future. Included in the legislation that was adopted by
the 145th convention was: the adoption of a master lia
bility insurance policy and a strict premium payment
enforcement procedure, determination and adoption of
an operating budget for the 1988-89 fiscal year, deter

mination of a policy strongly discouraging "little sister"
organizations in Psi Upsilon chapters, a review ofthe Psi
Upsilon Constitution, and the adoption of a new policy
for the acceptance of chapters into the fraternity.
The chairmen ofthe various legislative committees had
much work to accomplish during the three day event:
getting their committees organized, seeing that the leg
islation was written, and assuring that the work of the
committee was given careful consideration by the del
egates at large. These key people were: Charles M. Hall,
Nu Alpha '71, Committee on Budget and Development;
Edward G. Mitzen, Pi '89, Committee on New Business;
Murray A. Kahn, Theta Theta '90, Committee on Un
finished Business; John K. Menzies, Pi '41, Committee
on Credentials and Nominations; and Thomas A. Leg
